problem.title_as_question: What is fault tolerance in action and why is it essential to winning tennis matches?
problem.definition: Tennis players frequently get jammed or caught out of position against tough opponents, but winning matches requires maintaining contact in front to produce an acceptable shot rather than missing outright.

symptoms.description: The player is positioned too close to the incoming ball, leaving the arm unable to extend fully and the hips restricted.
The player finishes with an awkward swing above the head due to being cramped for space.
The ball is struck less cleanly than desired but still penetrates deep enough to keep the opponent defensive.
When jammed, a compromised shot either misses outright or floats passively back to the middle.

causes.statement: Suboptimal probing footwork causes the player to position themselves too close to the incoming ball.
Being jammed too close to the ball restricts arm extension and prevents natural hip rotation.
Playing against high-level opponents who hit hard and deep inevitably forces players out of ideal position.

angles.summary: Analyzing Holger Rune hitting an inside-in forehand under pressure against Cameron Norrie to illustrate fault tolerance in live pro play.
Even from an awkward body position with jammed hips, maintaining the same fundamental contact point in front allows an effective shot.
Contrasting Rune's jammed forehand with his perfectly prepared inside-out forehand showing full extension and weight transfer.
Matches are not won by having 10-20% higher peak shot quality, but by making compromised shots 80% as good instead of missing outright.
